html:
SMTO-SSH-0006 — SMTO couldn't confirm which computer and account SSH used

GUID: 705e77fe-87af-4d73-9308-0132e171a8bd
Slug: ssh-handshake-incomplete
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: ssh

What happened

  • SSH's record of the connection was missing details SMTO needs: the computer's address, the account, or proof that the computer's key was trusted. SMTO didn't save this connection for reuse.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether the command already did its job on the remote computer before running it again. SMTO checks this record after the command finishes, so a missing detail doesn't mean the command failed or didn't run.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to confirm it uses the standard OpenSSH program; running ssh -V there should mention OpenSSH. SMTO reads OpenSSH's own connection messages, and other SSH programs word them differently.
  3. Ask SMTO to run a harmless SSH command on that computer, such as one that prints the date, and see whether this message returns. If a simple command connects cleanly, the earlier problem was a one-off interruption during the connection.

What success looks like

  • A simple SSH command completes, and later commands to that computer run without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the output of ssh -V from the Gateway computer, to the person who manages it. Don't assume the earlier command didn't run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The captured OpenSSH DEBUG1 handshake log lacked one or more required lines: 'Connecting to … port', 'Authenticating to … as', 'Server host key: … SHA256:' or 'Host … is known and matches'.

What this means

  • SSH setup cannot find all required connection host/port, login account, server fingerprint and trusted-match markers in the captured handshake log. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • SSH setup cannot find all required connection host/port, login account, server fingerprint and trusted-match markers in the captured handshake log.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the missing marker and inspect the original command result separately from continuity evidence.

How to fix it

  • Observation._setup in src/gateway_core/ssh_context.py parses the -E DEBUG1 log. Confirm the Gateway uses a stock OpenSSH client (ssh -V) whose log contains the Connecting, Authenticating, Server host key and 'is known and matches' lines, and that no wrapper alters logging, then run a harmless verified ssh command to enroll. Do not treat the missing evidence or a lost connection as proof that the earlier remote command did not run.
  • Reconnect through the supported SSH flow and complete the handshake, then inspect its public host identity evidence before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported verified SSH operation produces complete correlated public identity evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
